Is AHPRA RN OSCE Online Module really a one-time payment?

Yes. You pay once and keep access for your first sitting and any resit, with content updates included.

How do I get access after I pay?

Create an account in the app with the same email you used at checkout. Your account is unlocked once your purchase is confirmed, and you'll see the full course the next time you sign in.

Is this the official Ahpra OSCE?

No. This is an independent study resource with original practice stations, not real exam items. Always follow the current NMBA candidate handbook.

What is the difference between the Online Module and the Face-to-Face Intensive?

The AHPRA RN OSCE Online Module (A$199) is the online app you study at your own pace. The Face-to-Face Intensive (A$1,950) includes that same online module, plus a 1-week in-person course in a hospital clinical simulation lab where an OSCE trainer observes you closely as you perform the stations.

Hands-on practice with an OSCE trainer watching every step

What is the difference between the Online Module and the Face-to-Face Intensive?

The AHPRA RN OSCE Online Module (A$199) is the online app you study at your own pace. The Face-to-Face Intensive (A$1,950) includes that same online module, plus a 1-week in-person course in a hospital clinical simulation lab where an OSCE trainer observes you closely as you perform the stations.

Why must the intensive be 2–3 weeks before my exam?

It leaves enough time to fix the feedback from your trainer while the hands-on practice is still fresh, without leaving it so long that you lose the rhythm of the stations.

Why are face-to-face places limited?

This is an intensive prep that needs close observation by the OSCE trainer. Keeping each intake to 8–10 students means everyone gets hands-on turns and individual feedback.

How do I pay for the face-to-face intensive?

Send us your full name and exam date using the form above. We'll confirm a place in the right intake and send you a secure Stripe payment link. Your spot is held once payment is received.

Safety & infection control

A client is receiving a blood transfusion and develops chills and low back pain 10 minutes after it starts. What should the nurse do first?

ASlow the transfusion rate
BStop the transfusion
CNotify the provider
Rationale: stop first to limit exposure, keep the IV line open with 0.9% saline, then assess and notify.

Adaptive exam

A full NCLEX-style adaptive exam

  • 01Every answer changes the next question: get it right and the next one is harder.
  • 0285 to 150 questions in 5 hours. It stops as soon as it is 95% sure of your result.
  • 03No rationales until the end, so it feels like test day.
  • 04Finish with a readiness report and your strongest and weakest areas.
Above averageAverageBelow average

Rationales that teach

Why each answer is right or wrong, the pathophysiology behind it and the bedside teaching point.

Memory hooks

A visual mnemonic on every question, collected in the Mnemonic Vault for quick review.

Test-taking strategies

Prioritisation, delegation and smart guessing, explained with games and examples.

OET Prep for nurses

The Occupational English Test is built for healthcare professionals, and it is one of the English tests the NMBA accepts for registration. We're building OET practice for nurses, using the clinical situations you already know.

IN DEVELOPMENTComing soon
Link coming soonHear first on Telegram
OET
The four sub-tests

What the OET tests

Nurses sit the Nursing version, so the tasks come from real healthcare settings.

ListeningConsultations and healthcare talks.
ReadingHealthcare texts, from short notices to articles.
WritingA letter, such as a referral or discharge letter, from case notes.
SpeakingRole-plays with a patient or carer.
NMBA minimum scores

The scores you need for registration

For OET tests taken on or after 23 April 2026.

ListeningReadingWritingSpeaking
350360350360

Tests taken on or before 22 April 2026 use the earlier minimums. Always check the current rules on Ahpra's accepted English tests page before you book.

English · PTE Academic

PTE Prep for nurses

PTE Academic is a computer-based English test taken at a test centre, and the NMBA accepts it for registration. We're building PTE practice designed for nurses working toward the English standard.

Questions

Before you start

Getting started

How do I get access after I pay?

Checkout is handled securely by Stripe. Create an account in the app with the same email you used at checkout. Your account is unlocked once your purchase is confirmed, and you'll see the full course the next time you sign in.

I'm preparing for both exams. Do I need two accounts?

Each app has its own sign-in. You can use the same email for both.

Can I use it on my phone?

Yes. Both apps work in your phone's browser, and the videos are filmed in portrait for phones.

Payments

Is AHPRA RN OSCE Online Module a one-time payment?

Yes. You pay once and keep access for your first sitting and any resit, with content updates included.

How does NCLEX Hero billing work?

Choose a monthly payment (A$42.99 each month) or pay every 3 months (A$84.99, about A$28.33 a month). Your plan renews automatically until you cancel, and you can cancel at any time.

How do I book the OSCE Face-to-Face Intensive?

Open the AHPRA RN OSCE Face-to-Face tab and send us your full name and AHPRA OSCE exam date on Telegram or WhatsApp. The intensive (A$1,950) includes the online learning module, runs for 1 week and must be completed 2–3 weeks before your exam. Places are limited to 8–10 students per intake, and we'll send your payment link once your place is confirmed.

About us

Is this affiliated with Ahpra, the NMBA or NCSBN?

No. NextGen Nurses is an independent study resource. The practice stations and questions are original teaching material, not real exam items. Always follow the current official candidate handbook for your exam.

When will OET and PTE prep be ready?

They're in development. Join the Telegram group to hear first when they open.
